item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-08-16
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-08-16 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal over the last 7 days (2026-08-09 to 2026-08-16). A moderate week — 12 shoulder-specific clinical and translational articles, with the JSES family again carrying the load (6 JSES, 3 JSES International) and headlined by a Rush propensity-matched comparison of anatomic arthroplasty with a posterior augmented glenoid against reverse arthroplasty for Walch B2/B3 disease, a Madrid matched-pair study of cement-augmented locking plates versus reverse arthroplasty for elderly proximal humerus fractures, and a Taiwanese randomized dose-response trial of extracorporeal shockwave therapy in adhesive capsulitis. Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and the Bone & Joint Journal each published no qualifying shoulder articles this week — their output was knee, hip, spine, and trauma. Letters, errata, author replies, editorials, and editorial commentaries were excluded, as were elbow-only items and articles already covered in earlier digests. Search note: the 7-day entry-date window was cross-checked against a create-date sweep back to 2026-07-20 to catch back-dated ahead-of-print records. That cross-check surfaced no additional includable shoulder articles — the shoulder-adjacent records it returned were all correctly excludable: the JBJS commentary on the Aleem lesser-tuberosity-osteotomy randomized trial (the primary article itself was covered in the 2026-08-08 digest), the AJSM "Rise of Remplissage" editorial and the Bankart letter/response exchange, two Arthroscopy editorial commentaries (rotator cuff retear strength predictors, patch augmentation), and five elbow-only papers (radial head arthroplasty designs, implant removal after failed radial head arthroplasty, total elbow arthroplasty for post-traumatic sequelae, elbow CT Hounsfield units, and capitellar osteochondral autograft). One JSES paper on distal biceps repair fixation was excluded as elbow-only. --- Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery (6) Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty with the Tornier Perform Posterior Augmented Glenoid versus Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for the Treatment of Walch B2 and B3 Glenoids: A Propensity Score Matched Analysis Harkin W & Garrigues GE (corresponding author Harkin W) — Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Rush University Medical Center, Chicago, IL, USA The week's most directly practice-relevant paper: a Level-III retrospective matched cohort drawn from a prospectively collected registry, comparing anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty with an all-polyethylene posterior augmented glenoid against reverse arthroplasty in patients with glenohumeral osteoarthritis, an intact rotator cuff, and a Walch B2 or B3 glenoid, operated 2017–2023 with minimum 2-year follow-up. item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-08-08
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-08-08 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal over the last 7 days (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-08). A quieter week than the last — 13 shoulder-specific clinical and translational articles, concentrated almost entirely in the JSES family (7 JSES, 4 JSES International), and headlined by a Washington University randomized controlled trial on subscapularis repair in reverse arthroplasty. AJSM, Arthroscopy, and the Bone & Joint Journal each published no qualifying shoulder articles this week — their output was knee, hip, spine, trauma, and arthroplasty of the lower limb. Letters, errata, author replies, editorials, and editorial commentaries were excluded, as were elbow-only items and articles already covered in earlier digests. Search note: the 7-day entry-date window was cross-checked against a create-date sweep back to 2026-07-25 to catch back-dated ahead-of-print records. That cross-check surfaced seven additional records, all of which were correctly excludable — two editorial commentaries, a JBJS commentary on Werthel's posterior acromial morphology paper (the primary article itself was covered in the 2026-07-26 digest), the orthobiologics consensus statement, two elbow-only papers, a hip lexicon, and the AJSM nerve-block network meta-analysis already digested on 2026-07-26. --- Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (1) Cost-Effectiveness of Rotator Cuff Repair With Concomitant Subacromial Decompression at Mid-Term Follow-Up: A Systematic Review and Economic Analysis Saad Berreta R & Srikumaran U — Department of Orthopedics, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA A Level-II economic and decision-analysis study pairing a PRISMA systematic review of Level I–II trials with at least 5-year follow-up and a decision-tree cost-utility model comparing isolated rotator cuff repair against repair plus subacromial decompression over a 5-year horizon: adding decompression came out cheaper ($33,448 vs $34,593) and marginally more effective (1.465 vs 1.454 QALYs), making it the dominant strategy with an incremental net monetary benefit of $1,695 and favored in 99.28% of 1,000 Monte Carlo simulations — driven almost entirely by a reduction in revision rates, and robust to burr costs up to $1,721 and up to 43.6 extra minutes of operative time. item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-08-01
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-08-01 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal over the last 7 days (2026-07-25 to 2026-08-01). A strong week — 21 shoulder-specific clinical and translational articles, led by an eleven-article JSES batch. Letters, errata, author replies, and editorials/editorial commentaries were excluded, as were elbow-only and non-shoulder items and one AJSM article (the nerve-block network meta-analysis) already covered in last week's digest. --- American Journal of Sports Medicine (3) Suprascapular Nerve Release Improves the Histological Healing Morphology and Biomechanical Strength of the Rotator Cuff in a Rat Chronic Massive Rotator Cuff Tear Model Zhang W & Sun Y — Department of Hand Surgery, Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University, Nantong, China A controlled laboratory study in a rat chronic massive rotator cuff tear model (bilateral supraspinatus/infraspinatus transection, repaired at 4 weeks) asking whether suprascapular nerve entrapment is an independent barrier to tendon healing: neurofilament-200 staining showed entrapment in 7 of 10 shoulders, and adding concurrent nerve release to repair (n=14 rats per group) produced significantly higher maximum load at 8 weeks and better histologic healing scores at both 4 and 8 weeks — preclinical support for considering release at the time of massive cuff repair. PubMed Mid- to Long-term Outcomes of Coracoclavicular Ligament Reconstruction for Acromioclavicular Joint Dislocations: A Systematic Review of Studies With Minimum 5-Year Follow-up Boufadel P & Li X — Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Boston University School of Medicine, Boston, MA, USA A Level-IV systematic review of 16 studies (326 patients, 327 shoulders; weighted mean age 37 years, 85% men, mean follow-up 98 months) of open and arthroscopic coracoclavicular ligament reconstruction for Rockwood III–V acromioclavicular dislocations: functional results were excellent regardless of approach or technique (mean Constant 93.1, ASES 93.1, VAS 0.6), with 93% satisfaction and 88% return to preinjury sport, no loss of coracoclavicular distance over time, and overall complication, recurrence, and reoperation rates of 11.9%, 5.2%, and 6.1% — though arthroscopic procedures and suture-button/synthetic suspensory constructs carried higher recurrence and implant-related complication rates. item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-07-26
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-07-26 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal. Thin week — window widened to 14 days. The standard last-7-days pull surfaced only a handful of new shoulder items (below the ~8-article threshold), so per program rules the window was widened to 14 days (roughly 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-26). Most of what that widened window returned had already been covered in last week's (2026-07-18) sweeper digest — that run pulled the large JSES/JSES-International batch — and those duplicates were removed here. What remains is 4 genuinely new, non-duplicate, shoulder-specific clinical articles, one each in AJSM, Arthroscopy, JAAOS, and JBJS Am. Letters, errata, author replies, and editorials/editorial-commentaries were excluded (a JSES letter/reply on pharmacoepidemiologic real-world-data methods, a JSES editorial on the future growth of shoulder arthroplasty, and three Arthroscopy editorial commentaries — orthobiologics, stiff patients after cuff repair, and lower trapezius transfer), as were non-shoulder items (elbow — dynamic nerve MRI modeling, triceps-sparing total elbow arthroplasty, K-NOW unlinked total elbow kinematics; and the usual hip/knee/spine/foot content these general journals carry). --- American Journal of Sports Medicine (1) Nerve Blocks for Shoulder Arthroscopy: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials With a Network Meta-analysis Hurley ET & Garrigues GE — Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Rush University Medical Center, Chicago, IL, USA A Level-I network meta-analysis of 63 RCTs (4,235 patients) comparing interscalene (ISB), suprascapular (SSB), and supraclavicular (SCB) blocks, combined block techniques, and general anesthesia alone for pain control after shoulder arthroscopy: interscalene block was the most consistent technique for reducing 24-hour opioid consumption (SUCRA 77.5%), while combined and alternative strategies (SCB+axillary at 2 h, SSB+costoclavicular at 6 h, SSB alone at 12 h) gave incremental pain-control advantages at specific early time points, with only modest separation from ISB by 24 hours. PubMed --- Arthroscopy (1) Comparable Midterm Outcomes for Ultrasound-Guided Needling Versus High-Energy Shockwave Therapy for Rotator Cuff Calcific Tendinitis: A Randomized Controlled Trial van Noort DM & van Noort A — Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Spaarne Gasthuis, Hoofddorp, Netherlands Five-year follow-up of an RCT in 82 patients (67, 82%, reassessed) with symptomatic rotator cuff calcific tendinitis (5 mm, Gärtner I–II) that had failed nonoperative care including a subacromial steroid injection, randomized to four sessions of high-energy extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT) or a single ultrasound-guided needling/lavage (UGN): both arms reached excellent midterm Constant-Murley scores (94.4 vs 93.3, p=0.67) with 94% meeting the MCID and no recurrence of treated deposits, though additional trea

item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-07-18

item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-07-18 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal. This is a sweeper catch-up run — the normal Saturday pipeline died partway earlier today, having already produced a full 12-article, JSES/JSES-International-only pull for the standard 7-day window (2026-07-12 to 2026-07-19) but under an incorrect date label. This digest corrects that label to the proper target date (2026-07-18) and, per program rules for a sweeper, re-checked a widened window (out to 30 days, 2026-06-18–2026-07-18) for anything additional — which surfaced 2 further genuinely new, non-duplicate shoulder-specific articles in AJSM and Arthroscopy that the narrower run had missed. Letters, errata, author replies, and editorials were excluded throughout (including a JSES letter/reply exchange on GLP-1 agonists and adhesive capsulitis, a JSES randomized trial on shoulder immobilization that PubMed tagged as a "Letter" with no abstract, and an Arthroscopy editorial commentary on lower trapezius transfer), as were non-shoulder items (elbow, hip, knee, foot/ankle, spine, and general orthopaedic-practice/innovation content — these journals cover far more than shoulder). 14 articles included this week. --- Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery (10) Development of Convolutional Neural Networks for Classification and Characterisation of Proximal Humerus Fractures on Computed Tomography Mennes SRJ & Jaarsma RL — Department of Orthopaedics and Trauma Surgery, Flinders Medical Centre and Flinders University, Adelaide, Australia In 581 Australian and 122 Dutch patients with proximal humerus fracture CT scans, a 3D convolutional neural network (DenseNet) classified fracture patterns with 78.6% accuracy and matched or exceeded orthopedic surgeons for greater tuberosity displacement, varus malalignment, shaft translation, and articular involvement, though some subclass performance remained insufficient for clinical use. item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-07-11 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal. This is a sweeper catch-up run — the normal Saturday pipeline did not execute this week, so this digest also backfills the gap. The last-7-days entry-date window (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-11) yielded only 2 genuinely new, non-duplicate shoulder articles, so per program rules the window was widened progressively to 14 days, then to 30 days (2026-06-11 to 2026-07-11), which surfaced a substantial backlog of shoulder-specific content — mostly in JSES/JSES International — not covered by the prior two (narrower-window) digests. Letters, errata, author replies, editorials, and non-shoulder items (elbow-only, hip, knee, wrist/hand, spine, general ortho-practice pieces) were excluded throughout. 27 articles included this week. --- Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery (11) Influence of Age-Related Bone Density Changes on Primary Stability in Stemless Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Multi-Implant Finite Element Study Líbano Monteiro H & Folgado J — IDMEC, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa, Lisbon, Portugal Finite-element modeling of five stemless anatomic implant designs found that age-related bone-density decline increased micromotion at the bone-implant interface, but several designs (Global Icon, Inhance) remained stable regardless of osseointegration threshold, suggesting age alone may not contraindicate stemless TSA. PubMed Evaluation of New Normal After Shoulder Arthroplasty: Comparison of Anatomic vs. Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Beleckas CM & Levy JC — Levy Shoulder to Hand Center, Paley Orthopedic and Spine Institute, Boca Raton, FL, USA Among 849 aTSA and 745 rTSA patients with ≥2-year follow-up, 40% of aTSA vs. 26% of rTSA patients reached a "new normal" (SANE ≥95), with aTSA patients significantly outperforming rTSA in higher-demand functions, work/sport return, and range of motion. PubMed Long-Term Outcomes of Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty Versus Nonoperative Treatment for 3- or 4-Part Proximal Humerus Fractures in Elderly Patients: Results From a Prior Randomized Clinical Trial Lopiz Y & Marco F — Clínico San Carlos Hospital / Complutense University, Madrid, Spain Long-term (mean 7.4–7.6 year) follow-up of the first RCT comparing RSA vs. nonoperative treatment for displaced 3-/4-part proximal humerus fractures in patients ≥80 years found RSA maintained better Constant scores over time as nonoperative outcomes deteriorated. item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-07-04
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-07-04 Pulled from PubMed across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal. The last-7-days entry-date window (2026-06-27 to 2026-07-04) was sparse for genuinely new shoulder content — most hits duplicated last week's digest — so the window was widened to 14 days (2026-06-20 to 2026-07-04) per program rules. Letters, errata, author replies, editorials, and non-shoulder items (elbow, hip, knee, wrist) were excluded. 16 articles included this week. --- Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery (10) Assistant Experience Enhances the Learning Curve in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Comparative CUSUM Analysis of Three Surgeons Taniguchi S & Terai H — Osaka Metropolitan University Graduate School of Medicine, Osaka, Japan CUSUM analysis of the first 60 rTSA cases for three surgeons found that prior high-quality assistant experience was associated with earlier stabilization of operative time, blood loss, and perioperative complications during the early learning curve. PubMed Prediction of Acromial and Scapular Spine Fractures After Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty using Machine Learning: A Retrospective Cohort Study Schneller T & Scheibel M — Schulthess Clinic, Zürich, Switzerland In a registry of 2,256 rTSAs, a logistic-regression machine-learning model using implant design and patient factors predicted acromial/scapular spine fracture risk (4.1% incidence) with fair accuracy (AUROC 0.71); medialized-distalized implant design, cuff tear arthropathy, older age, and osteoporosis were the strongest predictors. PubMed Simultaneous versus Staged Bilateral Shoulder Replacement: A Matched Cohort Study Pina G & Boileau P — ICR-Institut de Chirurgie Réparatrice, Clinique Kantys, Nice, France Matched-cohort study of 16 simultaneous vs. 32 staged bilateral shoulder arthroplasty patients found simultaneous surgery significantly shortened total length of stay (3.4 vs. 7.5 days) while achieving equivalent range of motion, satisfaction, and complication rates in carefully selected patients. PubMed The Humeral Bone Loss (HUMBL) Classification Identifies Patterns of Humeral Bone Loss Associated with Various Revision, Instability, and Humeral Loosening Rates in Primary and Revision Shoulder Arthroplasty Nieboer M & Frankle M — Florida Orthopaedic Institute / Tampa General Hospital, Tampa, FL, USA In 1,083 shoulders undergoing primary or revision arthroplasty, the new HUMBL classification found segmental, ectatic, and discontinuity patterns of humeral bone loss were associated with progressively higher rates of revision, instability, and humeral loosening. item.title: Shoulder Literature — 2026-07-03
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Weekly Shoulder Surgery Literature Digest — 2026-07-03 Pulled from PubMed, entry dates 2026-06-26 to 2026-07-03, across JSES, JSES International, AJSM, JAAOS, Arthroscopy, JBJS Am, and Bone & Joint Journal. Letters, errata, author replies, editorials, and non-shoulder items (5 hip, 1 wrist, 2 elbow-only) were excluded. 20 articles included this week. --- Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery (1) Factors Associated With Poor Outcomes For Female Patients Undergoing Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Wright MA & Zmistowski B — Washington University in St Louis School of Medicine, St. Louis, MO, USA In a retrospective study of 409 women who underwent anatomic or reverse total shoulder arthroplasty, 35% failed to reach a patient-acceptable symptom state at 2 years, with smoking, prior ipsilateral shoulder surgery, and reverse (vs. anatomic) arthroplasty independently predicting worse outcomes. PubMed --- JSES International (13) High retear rates despite clinical improvement after arthroscopic partial repair for large to massive rotator cuff tears Baek CH & Pham PT — Choray Hospital, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam Retrospective series of 142 patients undergoing arthroscopic partial repair for large-to-massive rotator cuff tears found significant functional gains at 26 months despite a 30.3% retear rate, with structural failure linked to worse outcomes. PubMed Video-enhanced informed consent improves patient comprehension in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial Scheidegger PD & Bouaicha S — Balgrist University Hospital, University of Zürich, Zürich, Switzerland RCT of 60 rTSA patients found a 2-minute pre-consent educational video significantly improved comprehension scores versus verbal discussion alone (5.70/7 vs 4.67/7), with the greatest benefit in older, less-educated, and non-native-speaking patients. PubMed The subacromial index: a novel radiological parameter associated with rotator cuff tears Üner Ç & Serbest S — Kırıkkale University Faculty of Medicine, Kırıkkale, Türkiye Retrospective imaging study of 132 shoulder MRIs proposes a new "subacromial index" measurement that remains associated with rotator cuff tears independent of age and acromial index, alongside established radiographic parameters. PubMed Long-term follow-up of functional electromyostimulation-augmented home exercise after primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty Wittmann T & Raiss P — OCM Clinic, Munich, Germany Follow-up of 10 patients from a prior RCT found that Constant Score and Subjective Shoulder Value gains achieved with a 6-week home electromyostimulation program after rTSA were maintained (and modestly improved) at a median 18 months, though the untreated control arm was not re-evaluated.
